purpose: The single ordered path that builds a database from zero. A script outside this path is never replayed as part of a build.
rules: The path is tiered: EF migrations, then Backend/database/scripts, then Backend/database/views.
Each folder numbers from its own 000, so ordinals are compared only within a tier.
Explicit adjudication beats filename heuristics. Every override records its reason.
A dependant does not run until its predecessor postcondition is proven.
Exactly one ordered path exists. This file is it.
Every SQL file carries exactly one disposition. There is no unknown state.
A new script joins this manifest in the same commit that creates it.
A table is created once on the path; any later create must be guarded by IF NOT EXISTS.
Demonstration, seed and test content is never on the path.
Read-model views are a separate authority applied after every schema script, and every view they declare must exist in the built database.
System templates are created by the runtime authority. SQL template scripts are migration history, not a second runtime authority.

Product tables live in ppiq_meta, ppiq_plant or ppiq_staging. A single terminal convergence file relocates them after every historical creator has run; no migration and no historical script moves a table.

storageTopology.note: Physical placement of product tables. The model half is StorageTopologyMap; the physical half is the terminal convergence file. Both are generated from one frozen assignment.

efMigrationBaseline.note: The schema baseline. Applied by dotnet ef database update before any SQL script; several scripts fail by name without it.

canonicalViews.note: Read-model view authority. Applied after every schema script and after topology convergence, before the probe database is dropped.

canonicalPath.reason: Canonical detail contract for the definition store.
T-231 durable Analysis Subject and Grain authority bound to canonical definition versions.
